extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships (immigrants and children of immigrants seeking graduate funding)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and selection standards for applicants seeking the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship for New Americans, describing eligibility, selection priorities, and program obligations/support for one-to-two years of graduate study in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria (creativity, originality, initiative, sustained accomplishment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection criteria emphasize creativity, originality, initiative, and sustained accomplishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship looks for applicants who demonstrate these qualities; selection decisions value those traits as primary merits. The page also pairs these criteria with an expressed interest in diverse perspectives and applicants across a range of fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to the Constitution and the Bill or Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are valued for a commitment to the Constitution and the Bill or Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This civic/values-oriented commitment is explicitly named as a value alongside creative and scholarly accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit-based selection; no quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition is merit-based. The program does not have any quotas for types of degrees, universities or programs, countries of origin, or any other factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is intended to be driven by the applicants' merit and accomplishments rather than prescriptive quotas by degree type, institution, country, or similar categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑discrimination in selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of Fellows from among eligible applicants is made without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship affirms equal-opportunity selection; protected characteristics must not influence awarding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — New American status (immigrants and children of immigrants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship is for New Americans — immigrants and children of immigrants. Eligibility has been broadened over time to include DACA recipients and, as of recent updates, 'all immigrants, regardless of their immigration status, who have graduated from both high school and college in the US.' Refugees and asylees need not wait for green cards to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should meet the program's definition of 'New American' as stated; historical expansions (2001, 2014, 2019) reflect increasing inclusivity. The page names immigrants, asylum seekers, and refugees as the populations the program supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed fields and degree programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship supports graduate study in any field and in any advanced degree-granting program in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no restrictions on field of study — applicants from screenwriting to medicine, physics to painting, law to neuroscience, opera to mechanical engineering have been supported. The program explicitly welcomes a diverse array of academic and professional pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and stage of support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship supports one to two years of graduate study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program funding is provided for one to two years. Historically (noted in the site history), policy allowed candidates to already be in graduate studies but not beyond their second year; that historical note may inform timing expectations for applicants but the current site language emphasizes one-to-two years of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program obligations and participation (conferences and campus contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows participate in two Fall Conferences in New York City (all expenses paid) and meet with the Fellowship director on their campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a Fellow includes membership in a lifelong community and participation in Fellowship-sponsored events and mentoring activities; applicants should expect engagement with the Fellowship community if selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community, alumni engagement, and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: New Fellows join an active alumni association (The Paul & Daisy Soros Fellows Association) and are part of a lifelong community that includes mentoring programs and regional events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship emphasizes ongoing alumni involvement (e.g., PDSFA, mentoring program, chair of PDSFA sits on the Board). Applicants should be prepared for communal and alumni-related activities and potential mentoring roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in diverse perspectives and interdisciplinary impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship states an interest in a diverse array of applicants and perspectives and highlights Fellows' potential to impact change and innovation across society, culture, and academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who can articulate how their background and work bring valuable or novel perspectives to their field and to broader civic life may align well with the program's stated aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication, age, and historical policy notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical policy changes noted: individuals could reapply; age-limit was raised from 28 to 30 at the upper end and eliminated at the lower end; interviews became bi-coastal; selection panels included graduated Fellows. In 2001 candidates could already be in their graduate studies, although not beyond their second year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These historical items reflect the program's evolution; applicants should consult current application instructions for up-to-date rules about reapplication, age limits, and stage-of-study eligibility, since site history documents prior policy shifts.
